review:
I picked this game up a long time ago, but never really got into it. Deciding to give it another try, I played through several of the missions, and these are my thoughts - 

The price is generally right. Good amount of bang for the buck here, great deal if you find it on sale. Good amount of playtime for the money you'll spend.

It tries to actually be a realistic sim. The other end of the spectrum is CoD, which is divorced from reality for the most part. Each approach has their merits, depends on what you're looking for. Here, the action is slower, you may or may not see who is shooting at you, etc. For being an older game, the graphics are still pretty decent.

The biggest issue I have with it is that it is very unpolished. The engine was developed as a training tool for real-world militaries, and it somewhat suffers the same fate as other programs which are developed for real-world training (think Ship Simulator, for one). Whoever is using it for training may or may not be a gamer, and probably doesn't have a lot of say in whether or not they use it, so they don't really care. Here, you have terrible AI at times, broken conversations, buggy objectives, awful dialogue, random music cues, and so on. You're not going to find a product which is geared toward an enthusiast gamer, and you're not going to find a product that would have been competitive in terms of polish even 8-9 years ago.

That being said, it's still an interesting game, and a change of pace from shooters that thrive on improbable situations and gameplay.

I've spent most of my hours playing Chernarus Life when it was still a thing that existed, usually on the Excyted Gaming servers (even if the admins were absolutely rеtаrdеd sometimes - fυсk you Eric). Regardless, I've played through the campaign, spent hours and hours at a time working with other players to liberate towns, outposts and encampments in Hohei Evolution Blue and Evolution Red on the Anzu's War Games servers. 

Eventually, after playing this game for a while, I purchased Operation: Arrowhead. The original ARMA 2 still had an enormous playerbase even though OA had been released for quite some time as well. I found myself enjoying ARMA 2 over OA any day. The fact that OA lacked Chernarus Life and replaced it with the less-good Takistan Life Revolution and Island Life was offputting for me, since those maps were less well suited for a civlian-vs-cops type scenario, whereas Chernarus was literally the perfect "Life" map.

ARMA 2 was a bit clunky in the controls, but once you got them down (or simply adjusted the keybindings in the options menu) the game was such a blast to play. I probably spent about 50 hours in the mission editor alone, creating my own little missions and scenarios to play through with friends or on my own. 

I won't get in to the specific features of the game itself, because now that the multiplayer is gone nobody will ever be able to experience the game in its full potential again. The game is entirely dead now due to the GameSpy shutdown, which hosted ARMA 2 servers, but you can still play multiplayer in Operation Arrowhead. That being said, this game was absolutely fantastic.

 10/10 from me, even though it had some bugs and a few odd things here and there, that's what made it ARMA 2. ARMA 3 doesn't come close to this game. Not only does ARMA 2 have more guns and vehicles than ARMA 3, but the mission editor is much better as well. So, for my conclusion?

Don't buy this game. It would have made a great purchase any time before 2014, because the multiplayer still worked and there was a huge fanbase with a wide variety of servers and community-created addons that made the game so much better. ARMA 2 is now just a mediocre single-player campaign. For $12.99 USD (price as of August 12, 2016) this game is absolutely not worth it. 'Do you recommend this game,' Steam asks me. I do, emphatically. I hope this anecdote from an in-game multiplayer experience I had will explain why. Prepare yourself for [u]ARMA2: The Review: The Movie.[/u]

Spring, 2011; early in my ARMA career, first tour of duty after a Steam Sale. I'm a fairly fresh recruit, seasoned with a couple dozen game-hours spent trudging through an expansive and swampy learning curve. Spent today at work, drove home, made dinner, cleaned up; it's Game-O'clock. Steam. ARMA2. Launch. Menu surfing, looking for multiplayer. Server browser hits my face with lists of information. -AWP-Warfare [i]Capture the Island[/i] mode looks appealing tonight. Played it a couple times before, and I feel comfortable with the basics by now. Server connection established.

Click! I'm in, filling the boots of a digital NATO badass. Apparently, international treaty organisations occasionally require the service of men with guns. Disturbing thought, but I'm no politician. I'm just a nobody with a rifle, taking orders that filter down the food chain. Those orders fill my mind now. Objective: town. Location: nearby...as the crow flies. Heh, the team's commander [i]does[/i] have airborne technology unlocked, I just don't have the cash to buy a lift yet. Looks like I'm taking the scenic route. A quick check of my map tells me I'm at one of our hidden frontier bases and that there's two whole mountains between me and the nearby town. Great... I'll be taking the scenic route to the scenic route. The map tells me more: several of my team members and their A.I. controlled task forces are currently approaching the town. I'm already late for the party :(

Might as well bring the fireworks.

The base I'm at has only an armour factory and infantry barracks, but both will well suit my rapidly forming battle plan. I'm thinking heavy calibre fire support from high ground, overlooking the town. The topographic information in the map shows that the road I'll be taking is nestled around a minor hill as it approaches the town. Perfect. I'll park two BMPs there and they'll provide overwatch of the whole area while my comrades finish their capture of the town. An LAV will ferry me and one squad of A.I. infantry to the combat zone. I spend the required funds and set the plan in action.

Wait a tick, BeatYourHeadIn, are you telling me you actually have to plan how you’re going to get your troops and equipment from point A to point B in ARMA2? Logistics in a game!? Yes, actual logistics... in a game with a map so FRIGGIN big you need to employ logistical planning skills to see any sort of success. And it's not boring!

Back to the story. Formation of a military convoy. A few orders issued to my A.I. controlled task force later and the BMPs are on point while I lounge in the command chair of the LAV at the rear of the column. I man the turret-mounted automatic grenade launcher, a devastating weapon. Its barrel is ominously pointed at and tracking a lollygagging friendly player as my convoy departs base. [i]Yeah, that's right chump, make one wrong move and I'll end you![/i] Though itching to test the power of my new toy, I decide it's not worth getting banned over.  I let my teammate live, for now.

The A.I. drivers of my convoy are as dim as a new moon, but I can fine tune my plans and keep up with current events while they drive. It's an 10 to 15 minute (realtime) drive that negotiates a winding mountain pass through an elegant evergreen forest. These are backroads, unpaved; enemy forces unlikely to be using this route. I feel secure enough that I spend most of the trip looking at the map, reading topography, lanes of fire, positions of friendlies. I smile when I realize I could probably minimize ARMA2 and play a few rounds of Counterstrike while my convoy travels.

Dying immediately is certainly the last thing I'm worried about as I crest the peak of the second mountain.

Suddenly: EXPLOSION..DEAFENING SOUND..FROM BEHIND..MASSIVE DETONATION..JESUS H. CHRIST WHERE IS THAT VOLUME KNOB! What is going on here!?

My turret pans to the rear of the LAV. The sight, what a sight...I'll never forget. Fire. Wall. 60? 70 feet tall? A wall. Of fire. Taller than the trees in the forest, literally FILLS my view from left to right. There is nothing in view except the fire. I'm in awe. Confused. Shaken. I've seen 'splosions in this game before, BUT NEVER LIKE THAT! Did somebody tried to nuke me FFS!? I know there's no nukes in this game mode, so...

Over the cacophany of destruction: the scream of jet engines. Very close. As the flames die down, a large shape traverses the air over the crest of the crag. Airframe, Sukhoi configuration. Enemy. Wing tilted down slightly; canopy visible. I know he's surveying the carnage below him. Hunting me. Cursing his aim when he sees the LAV still intact. I feel small, molecule small; what I just witnessed was caused by his war machine. Napalm bombs. Heavy ordinance. Whatever it was, it dealt complete destruction to that forest.

Understand this, readers: in this game, air superiority is a literal phrase. Air is SUPERIOR in this game. This isn't your Battlefield "oh look I can shoot a few rockets from my jet fighter and maybe kill one or two goofs on the ground and then reload (because reloading rockets on a flying jet makes a lot of sense) and kill a couple more goofs" experience. No! In ARMA your aircraft can have a payload of more than a hundred devastating rockets and you can fire 'em full auto like a machine gun and destroy an entire town worth of goofs on the ground if you wanted to. Ha! Forget about balance! This is the real life Shiznit. Modern air forces don't invest heavily in war planes because they're "balanced". They invest in them because they can kill a hell of a lot of people quickly! ARMA2 knows this. Simply put, the developers have a big Bohemian boner for air power.

But BeatYourHeadIn, what happened next? Tell us! Okay, I'll tell you. A miracle happened. My convoy survives the 'splosion to end all 'splosions. My battle plans go up in smoke like the forest around me. My current objective is to live through the next 30 seconds. The LAV is the only reason I'm still alive. It is damaged, but drivable. I order my drivers to haul ass in a forwardly direction. I track the Sukhoi as the convoy labours onward. The receding bogey performs a wide highspeed U-turn. He's heading straight for me again. Relentless much? He's the UPS guy we all wished was real: the one who comes back after he missed you the first time, instead of leaving a note telling you to pick up your package at the office near the airport!

Then, from beyond the first mountain I had passed: a smoke trail racing skywards. Anti-aircraft missile! Ha! RETURN TO SENDER, A-HOLE! Two vectors intersect in a puff of smoke and light. Direct hit! Booyah! Wait, uh... he's still flying at me. HEY! HE'S STILL FLYING AT ME!

With black smoke billowing out of his engines, this topgun is still determined to deliver my severance package. Frantically, I order the BMPs to target the limping jet. Cannon rounds arc through the sky in attempt to smite the airborne menace. Sukhoi Dude is getting closer, but he's losing altitude. Fast. He's now descending below my level on the mountain, looking up at me through the trees as he approaches. None of the BMP fire connects, but it doesn't matter. THIS GOOSE IS COOKED BOYS! Relief. Now, his desperation salvo of rocket fire is way off-target; falls harmlessly some distance away. I watch him frantically yaw right and nose up as his fighter loses the last of its life-sustaining lift and plummets in a sideways cartwheel into the trees. The inferno he leaves behind is a feast for the eyes. There was nothing left but a dark crater.
Now, I can start thinking about that town again...

What, are you apes gonna dig him a grave!? We got our own mission to die for! Forward march!

All that's left to say is: play this game!

I'm going to try and keep this simple and to the point. I am not much for words but I'll try to condense what I think about this game.

Pros:
1. Huge potential. Large seamless maps. You can drive, fly or run across km after km. Towns, roads etc.. Basically entire detailed islands.
2. Great military sim taking advantage of the above. Realistic damage from small arms as well as vehicle weapons.
3. Lots of realistic military vehicles and aircraft. Even boats.
4. Multiplayer is fun, especially coop.
5. Speaking of multiplayer, Dayz mod is something special. Very fun and you can waste hours and hours in it.
6. The single player story is alright, I guess. Nothing to tell mom about.

Cons:
1. Bugs, glitches, more bugs. Absolutely unbearable, game breaking, punch your monitor and throw your computer out the window kind of bugs. Because you can only save 2 times per mission and the mission mught be very well broken before your first save and you won't know it until the end, which can take 1 hour or more if you take your time like me. All sorts of bugs. AI pathfinding drives your teammates vehicles off of cliffs. Mission scripts break and you can't complete the mission. You may fall through the floor and injure yourself badly or die (especially annoying in Dayz). I could write pages detailing the bugs, you get the idea.

2. Second most annoying thing is the interface and the interaction system. You have to scroll through a list of actions to change your weapon, get in a vehicle or perform some other mundane function which shouldn't be that complicated. There's a key for everything and then some. It's very clunky, slow and prone to you pressing the wrong button or doing something unintended. Controling your squad mates and telling them where to go, what to attack is tedious at best.

3. Clunky player movement? Even cars drive like crap and those are the easiest to control.

4. Inaccurate helicopter controls. Don't even get me started, whatever you read on the net, trust me. The heli controls are bad and make no sense. I have no idea what they were thinking when they decided that the helicopter would start acting like and airplane above 50 mph. I can fly no problem in flight sims and the Battlefield series. I even fly RC in real life. This is innacurate, plain and simple.

5. Devs had plenty of time to address these bugs/issues and this is a problem. What a bunch of underachievers. Their strategy is like this: For every new iteration/expansion, focus on adding more crap and complexity built on the same shoddy engine/interface and ignore all the bugs. Then collect money and develop the next uncooked iteration.

Arma2:OA isn't that much better, either. The missions bugs are fewer, but everything else is the same.

The bottom line: This is the kind of game you play because you know what to expect and you still want to play it because there isn't anything like it. You have to be a cult follower, or else you will hate it. The main reason you might get this is to play Dayz mod, which is great, but expect to be killed falling through floors, off ladders, killed by zombies walking through walls, etc... Definitely not for the casual gamer.

So I booted up ARMA 2 expecting a military shooter. What I got was a full-blown war simulator that makes real life seem arcadey. This game is so realistic I filed for VA benefits after a training mission.

Let me walk you through my first mission:

I spawned in.

My commander barked 47 acronyms at me in 10 seconds.

I opened the map, got lost, and closed it.

Walked 45 minutes through a forest to reach the objective.

Got shot in the leg by a bush. Or a sniper. Honestly not sure.

Bled out while trying to figure out how to crouch.

10/10 experience.

The controls? Oh, friend. ARMA 2 has one keybind for every action known to mankind. Want to go prone while aiming and checking your watch? That’s Ctrl+Shift+Alt+Q+Sneak+RealizeYouShouldHaveJoinedTheNavy.

The AI is a masterpiece of chaos. Sometimes your squadmates expertly flank an enemy bunker. Other times they run face-first into a tree and shout “CONTACT!” at a cow.

Also, if you love bugs, have I got a treat for you. One mission had my helicopter pilot land directly into the ocean while yelling “GO! GO! GO!” We all drowned, but at least we did it tactically.

But I’ll be honest: when it all works, it’s the most intense, immersive, pants-wettingly stressful experience ever. You feel like part of a real unit. Until Gary from logistics runs you over with a tank while yelling “I THOUGHT REVERSE WAS R!”

Final Rating: 7 invisible enemies out of 5

I grab my rifle. One last day. I run to the sarge. One last fight. I board the huey and we take off to the island of chernarus.

This review is all done after initially playing about 5 hours of said game.

I don't believe I have ever had a more confusing experience. I really wanted to like this game. It's extremely ambitious in design and looks pretty solid in areas. Modes such as Armory are relatively fun and grand in scope; however, playing the game is a frustrating experience. 

The controls are very strange and do not come to the player easily. You have to fiddle around with it to get it to your liking, which is easier said than done. Think about most first person shooter games with their controls: now remove aspects of sensitivity and general feeling of control on the weapon. I had a problem on more than one occassion where I died because I could not aim at the enemy at all. After going through the control menu, I selected a lock-on control scheme. The only way I could manage to hit anything is with this mode, and I'm questioning if I am simply stupid or the game is too buggy. Another problem I have is picking up weapons; it's very slow, and causes certain games (DayZ) to be incredulously hard to play because you end up getting caught off guard trying to get a weapon that you can't aim anyway.

 There are multiple views (third and first), and first person view is relatively hard on the eyes as the head bob on it is ridiculous (you can set it lower); I find myself more comfortable with the third person view, which gives a bigger picture anyway.

The worst thing I encountered in ArmA II (or any of its other games) is that it simply isn't fun. I never felt like anything was going to plan, that almost everything I did was hindered by the control. Perhaps if I had a controller, the game would respond better. Another big deal is the bugs within the game; they constantly appear, from minor ones as texture problems to really big bugs such as your helicopter flipping over randomly to kill you, lock the screen, and cause you to bring up task manager to get out of the game.

The frustration does not end there for me. I also wanted to get in on the DayZ Mod, which conveniently has a download on Steam. This download is not an updated version however, and is completely and utterly incompatible with 99% of online DayZ servers. So, you have to download a completely separate mod, DayZ Commander, to update all of your ArmA II games/DLC and also download updates to the DayZ mod, and then you can finally play a game. Great, right?

Wrong. Most servers seem to require something called "DayZ Epoch", another mod of a mod that you need to download. An extra 400mb on.

So you get that done, and you're ready. It's too bad that the mod has the exact same flaws as ArmA II that I listed above. I struggle to hit ANYTHING, and if I don't have a weapon, finding one while zombies attack you is next to impossible. The atmosphere is pretty cool, and the immersiveness is great, but it just doesn't seem to work at all for me. 

I do note here that the creators of ArmA II did not create the DayZ mod, but I have it here for reference due to the fact a great deal of players buy this game to play this mod.

In conclusion, I do not recommend this game; I dislike it for many reasons. If you feel like you can deal with a lot of frustration and can look past multiple issues within a game, then this is for you. I wanted to love this, as it offers a lot, but my experience with it has been bad and I wish it wasn't.

Wait until your friend gifts you this, or try it out before you spend your money. Don't regret buying a game you cannot refund.

This is the Mil Sim game. If you want to feel as close to a real war or shoot out as possible this is the game you want to play. The game vanilla isn't to bad but arma 2 is best with ACE or some other mods or custom missions. 

Once you play Arma you understand what a mil sim or tacitcal game is and what it isn't. Run forward like an idiot and you die, hide and you die, look the wrong way and you die. Very little hand holding and its wonderful. Its a game that attempts to recreate a warzone while still retaining some fun. 

If you buy Arma 2, pick up Operation Arrowhead with it because alot of mods like Dayz (I hate that garbage) require it or are better with it.

Hooking up with a nice milsim group and you will have alot of operating fun. The only disadvantage is that Arma 3 is out so 2 is on the way out. Even with only another freind or player or two Escape Chernarus is a wonderfull mission especially with ACE.

Graphics, Gameplay, its all good and intuitive. AI can be very impressive with ACE, vanilla AI can be very cumbersome and slow though but once they do react it can be quite impressive. Though there are alot of glitches here and there one thing to remember is its a mil sim, not a driving simulator or what have you.

Although Arma 3 has come out, I still think this game with Operation Arrowhead has potentional. Yet made for multiplay its singleplayer is  very dynamic. The fact is that this is a great first person shooter. Realism is hard to balance for some games but Bohemia did great with its game content allowing players to be able to counter anything thrown at them. I'd recommend this to anyone who enjoys a lot of game content for a unique fps.
